flags.json.description: Where flags go for every aos-* command (anywhere after their level, or before the first argument), help levels and short names.

errors.json.description: Read the program name, error code and reason before choosing whether to retry.

safety.json.description: Check the chosen daemon, agent and stack before destructive commands; scripts do not get a confirmation prompt.

agent.json.description: Use aos-agent ctl to attach (add), list, inspect, stop, sleep, pause, find and remove agents.

talk_settings.json.description: Use aos-agent say, listen, chat, open, close, watch, tools, llm and system to talk to one agent and change its overlays without modifying its definition.

history.json.description: Use aos-agent history to list, delete, summarize or replace messages in one agent's conversation.

hook.json.description: Use aos-agent hook to list, add or remove the hooks of one agent (including on_clock timers).

goal.json.description: Use aos-agent goal to give one agent a goal it is reminded of when it stops by itself; get, set, done, pause, resume, clear.

mailbox.json.description: Use aos-mailbox to see your mailbox folder, peek, read and send mailbox letters from a shell.

daemon.json.description: Use aos-daemon-ctl for any proc on one daemon (add, stop, sleep, pause, ls, ping, shutdown, prune, sweep); it bypasses the judge.

tools.json.description: Use aos-tools to edit a registry and call a registered tool with JSON on stdin.

tool_env.json.description: Save hub locations at registration time so each tool call uses the intended services.

tool_flags.json.description: Lib tools accept schema-derived flags as another way to supply their JSON input keys.

grow.json.description: Use aos-grow to move a function one level up (inline to file to folder) or down; preview with --dry-run.

eca.json.description: aos-eca-turn answers one turn of an external coding agent (claude, codex); aos-eca-screen opens, closes or watches its screen.

clock.json.description: aos-clock moves a clock file one cycle forward; aos-clock-register adds letters the clock sends every N cycles.

mcp.json.description: Use aos-mcp to serve the tools of an aos-tools registry to an external agent (Claude Code, codex) over MCP stdio.

mcp_import.json.description: Use aos-mcp-import to freeze the tools of an external MCP server into its server file, stack it in tools.json, and refresh it with sync; what its error codes mean.

sandbox.json.description: Use aos-sandbox to run a program in a sandbox: which paths it sees, network, limits, user.

sweeper.json.description: aos-sweeper runs one cleanup round for a daemon: archive big stderr files, expire archives, stop orphaned loops.

feedback.json.description: Use aos-feedback to record what was hard about a command or tool and to score how comfortable it is for AIs.

parts.description: Low-level programs the other commands are built from: aos-exec, aos-loop, aos-fsm, aos-daemon, aos-post, aos-lock, aos-json, aos-directive, aos-llm, aos-llm-kernel.

_description.json.description: Commands for humans and external agents: prefer registered tools inside aos, how the daemon and the agent are chosen, and which page to read first.
